inconsistencies: #34038, #35387 and #35355 all rework trace-logging configuration and the logging RPC. They are one decision, not three: review #34038 first (it carries the approach NACK that names #35387) together with #35387; #35355 duplicates the -trace/logging-RPC parts on top of an unrelated atomics change and should follow whichever design wins.

HTTP server cluster: #35780, #36200, #36204, #36259, #36276, #36124, #36159, #36198 all touch httpserver/httprpc connection handling. #36276 closes a loophole left by merged #36123 and #36124 completes encapsulation left by merged #35829; reviewing the bug fixes (#36259, #35780, #36276, #36204) before the refactors (#36124, #36159, #36198) avoids re-basing the fixes onto moving code.

#35837 and #35728 are the same defect class: an RPC reporting success or 'not found' when the node actually could not read the data. Review #35837 first, its trigger (index still syncing) is far more common than a disk I/O error.

#33904 and #35909 both extend REST under the parity effort tracked in #33808; #35909 also deduplicates boolean query-parameter parsing, so it should land first and #33904 should adopt that helper rather than adding its own parsing.
#27052 and #31672 both add per-peer diagnostic fields to getpeerinfo and bitcoin-cli -netinfo; review together so the field naming and clock/unit conventions match.
#35355 also overlaps #34038 on the RPC deprecation fallback for -loglevel; if #34038 merges, that part of #35355 is redundant work.
result.notes: The band spread is intentionally wide: one clear P1 (local RPC credential exposure), a small P2 set of interface security and returned-data correctness fixes, a large P3 middle, and a P4 tail of internal refactors, test-only and doc-only changes. The P3 band is large because this category has many independent small interface gaps of genuinely similar weight; within it I ordered correctness and reliability fixes ahead of new methods and fields, per the category's stated ordering, which is why several new-RPC PRs moved down from their solo positions and several small bug fixes moved up.
